text: Some nights she can’t sleep, and when the sun is gone, she has to look for him elsewhere. She lays down in front of the television in her underwear, the soft glow of its light radiates a cool warmth that sends shivers down her body.                                They listen to music together and talk about life because sometime life is all there is to talk about. They confront her about how much time she’s spending with him. This can’t be good for you, and she tries to understand their concern. She laughs at odd moments, as if her wiring is misfiring. She doesn’t try to rationalize or explain away. Part of her hopes they understand, but realizes that most don’t care to look where she looks, she doesn’t so much as say, but smile in their general direction. Why are you so happy, is the thing they can’t bring themselves to say, which she wants to respond to in so many ways, when they finally do. You’re doing funny things to me, she says one night, alone with her light. I’m burning you, he says.  I know you’re out there with so many others right now. I don’t feel very special. You’re the only one speaking to me, he says.  We had such a good time together, in that other place. Here, the people I care about are all trying to tell me something.  Perhaps you should listen to them, he says. I like far more what you have to say to me, and they’re just jealous because my time is valuable. Oh it most very is. She sleeps

She had had this bad accident, which is how she met him. A soft glow of light, his voice called out to her and she eagerly followed. She emerged into a world that was much like her own, only fundamentally very different. The rules of the place were dissimilar to the reality she called home, the very light itself played tricks in ways her eyes were unaccustomed to recieving. She strained to follow this ball of light because soon it was the only comfortable thing she knew. He led her deeper into his world, uncomfortable with the edges of things, wandering as if drunk off the stuff of life itself. The strange thing being, the more she looked into him, the closer she saw herself going home again, as if this was all a dream.                              From which she wakes, sheets pulled tight around her body. She strains and finds she can’t move , she is terrified, she’s felt this before, this terror, this sleep paralysis. Only then an arm is touching her, her mother’s looking down. The look on her face, the joy of this moment not betraying the horror of something else.  She can’t roll away from what comes next, she can only look at the ceiling, eyes searching the tears of light across the curve of her eye for the voice, for the way out of here.                          Just the barest of glimpses, but there he is. She gets the feeling that he’s been searching for her, aching just to be next to her. But she can’t be with him, not now, because of what’s happened to her. What’s happened to her. When all she wants to do right now is ask him, who are you?                 He responds as politely as he can.                 Just a point of light, looking for you, wanting to find you, with all my being.                                                                              All we are is light, she says.       And voice, carried oh so far.          I want to touch you, she says.                               Her mother looks down on her, the room filled with other people now.              That may not be wise now, he says. But look for me, come find me. This world of yours is most inviting.              How about we explore it together?               Yes, we will. But what will they think?             I’m only a secret if you make me a secret.                  Then I won’t.           Her mother’s frown matches her own smile.                    She puts her forefinger to her lips, grin pressed wide.

My sun-block lotion is orange and pink and here is where I can daydream I’m at my desk, waiting for the hour to dissolve away and my future open up like the sky falling down.

Products of the imagination. Distributed friendships, emergent acquaintances, proffered contact lists. I skim the rolodex and remove hazy recollections, broken trusts, go-betweens. My fingers scream for mercy. I type a form letter to payroll attorneys I’ve never seen. I don’t trust my eyes.

The parking garage is the color of honeydew. The fluorescent lighting plays against the concrete hardtop interior. The hum in the air is like electricity on the teeth. My throat warbles just a bit, a taste of unease swallowed away. Always the sound of the far off car descending that stresses me to action at a hurried pace. To retreat before it shows itself. The headlights catching me, the descending thing ever nearer.

An expense report I fill out. With gas mileage to and from lunch meetings, toll fares, printer cartridges, black markers and highlighters. Receipts of who owes what again. I do the math and the numbers leave my fingers connecting the past to the future. I feel the subtraction, the reduction of myself. Orange. Like a cream soda. I break down what I know and what I don’t. A list I keep hidden in my desk drawer. The Nieto Avenue Library. Monica Dewitt. Calamari. Sometimes, to help myself, I draw lines between the disparate associations, to try and make sense of it all.

I started wearing glasses when I turned twenty five. I look fine, I thought I wouldn’t when I was eighteen. My body changes almost daily. I degauss more often than I should. The wash of color, the breaking of the lines, the bending of the window, the reality I know. Like someone threw a pebble in.

There is a man who comes up to my desk once a week and tries to sell me cookies. His name is Javier and he talks about nothing but animals. Mammals, insects, fish and invertebrates, he organizes classifications of life in his mind like sports scores or famous quotations, sea cucumbers and pygmy shrews. What they have in common, how they’re completely unlike. Javier once told me that all cities are one city. That in your head exist all your ancestors, alive and fighting to live a new life through you.

I stay to work after hours, when the cleaning crews come over to play. In their white smocks and aprons, like chefs and surgeons, they chitter and chatter in foreign tongue and made up playspeak. Their hum can be heard above and below. Moving closer, then further away. The sound they make is the sound of alien lovemaking.

The white noise of penetration, their faces brittle and full of hostile intent. I stare at where the walls meet, at a ninety degree angle. How bright it is in the center, at the nexus. My eyes play tricks on me. I don’t trust them anymore, perhaps the lenses are too thick, the layers compressed together to fool me just so. Hidding inside is a polarized portal that hides and reveals things it should not.

There is a beach I visit where the waves crash thick white and the sand is blue. Volcanic rock I pack in bags and take home with me. Only the locals know of this place and they tend to avoid it. When the sun hits the horizon you’ve never seen anything like it. I only wade out to my knees. The kelp ropes around my ankles and black green crabs pump across the surface sideways.

My own personal refresh rate is set to the constant of the rate of decay of the universe. How often the new and beautiful washes over the old and stale Dorian Gray. Recreation on a conscious level extrapolated with the purely cosmetic zed. Beauty as a quantifier, measure it just so across matrices. Brow lines, beatific blemishes, jaw lines, ear placement, the tiny human dabs of paint that stick out to turn your head to the side in consideration.

I blow up letters. I place a form letter in the copying machine. Reduction is good for abstraction before re-enlargement. The letter e. lower case like e.e. cummings, filling eight and a half by eleven. It hardly looks perfect, inelegant but beautiful. Takes me twelve copies at four hundred percent to get it this large. The edges are jagged just right. Splotchy islands exist outside the mainland. Reason being who gives a shit. Forget for a second I have a reason to exist. I occupy my time setting goals, fulfilling milestones. Some of these I’d prefer to complete before I die.

I imagine my mortal coil like a corkscrew. As some higher power forces me through the cork, everything slows, I dull to a stop, then pop. My destiny fulfilled, my purpose accounted for by cosmic reckoning. I order lunch for the office. I account for coworkers indebted to me and the change I must break. I’m the day’s mealtime bookie. Today is Saigon Deli. A notepad of numbers and exceptions to the rule, none of this, more of that please. I daydream because it’s one of the few pleasures in life I don’t have to share with anyone. I’m selfish that way. I close my eyes when no one is looking.

My fingers bleed. The fingernails are bent back but never broken. They never speak to me. When one is not working on me, they shuffle together like they’re trying to dance. There is no music, only light that could almost be music, the way it pulsates and throbs. They look like neighbors. The class of people who live on the edge of what we know, are comfortable with.

Under the nails they place a thin strip of magnesium that sparks when it touches the pink wet. It burns like how agony would burn, I shake and weep and can’t control my legs which would kick up and at them. I see pink, soft and beautiful. Their caul is pulled across my vision.
